headline: South Asia: PM Shehbaz reaffirms support for Saudi Arabia in meeting with new envoy
script:
Good evening. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: PM Shehbaz reaffirms support for Saudi Arabia in meeting with new envoy.
- India: Saudi-Led Coalition Intercepts Drones, Missiles Targeted At Riyadh.
- Western Russia: One killed, six injured and buildings damaged in Russian attacks on Ukraine's west and centre – video.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: US Army’s 8th Psychological Operations Group inactivated.
- Military Times, 5 hours ago: US Army’s 8th Psychological Operations Group inactivated.
The Army's 8th Psychological Operations Group inactivated as the service reshapes its PSYOP and information warfare forces to counter global adversaries.
- Military Times, 13 hours ago: What is the US Army doing in Panama? A bit of everything..
As Washington shifts its attention toward the Western Hemisphere, a reinvigorated jungle school is just one part of the evolving U.S. presence in Panama.
- Military Times, 9 hours ago: ‘Weaponized light’: KBR’s new base defense technology pits lasers against drones.
The Pentagon recently selected KBR's Firefly system for a pilot program to test defending U.S. military installations against adversarial drones.
The Caribbean - bottom line: 19-y-o charged with Kidd Lane triple murder.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 18 hours ago: 19-y-o charged with Kidd Lane triple murder.
A 19-year-old man has been charged with three counts of murder in connection with last Friday’s deadly attack on Kidd Lane, off Spanish Town Road in St Andrew, which claimed the lives of two women and a one-year-old boy. The accused, Dante Davis, who has addresses on Spanish Town Road and Kidd Lane in Kingston 13, is also facing charges of conspiracy to commit murder, arson, conspiracy to commit arson, possession of a prohibited weapon, unauthorised possession of ammunition and using a firearm to commit a felony.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE

- Ukrainska Pravda, 9 hours ago: One killed, six injured and buildings damaged in Russian attacks on Ukraine's west and centre – video.
Regional authorities have reported strikes on Rivne, Kovel, Vinnytsia and Prykarpattia, resulting in power cuts, infrastructure fires and five injuries.
- The Moscow Times, Ukrainska Pravda, The Hindu - International, 6 hours ago: Russia Repels 644 Ukrainian Drones as Trump Calls Attacks on Russian Refineries ‘Disgrace’.
Russian strikes also left 370,000 residents in Ukraine’s northwestern Volyn region without electricity.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 7 hours ago: Russian General Staff announces start of massive strikes on Ukraine's energy grid.
Valery Gerasimov has stated that Russian forces have begun large-scale attacks on Ukrainian energy facilities amid ongoing power supply disruptions.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 8 hours ago: Zelenskyy and Finnish PM discuss Russian strikes and Ukraine's need for shelters.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo have discussed enhancing civil protection, building shelters and countering Russian attacks.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Democracy Digest: Polish Man Charged With Plotting to Kill PM, Suspected Saboteurs Arrested.
- Balkan Insight, 17 hours ago: Democracy Digest: Polish Man Charged With Plotting to Kill PM, Suspected Saboteurs Arrested.
Elsewhere, Slovakia to revive cooperation with Russia at meeting planned for November 25; Hungary parliament approves new child protection legislation; and Czech Army chief warns of possible Russian attack
- Politico Europe, 10 hours ago: Zelenskyy warns 20M Ukrainians could flee to Europe if Russia wins war.
The stark warning comes as Kyiv heads into a brutal winter and faces a cash crunch.
- Politico Europe, 10 hours ago: Denmark, Italy, Poland urge EU leaders to harden stance on irregular migration.
Draft conclusions backed by Rome, Warsaw and Copenhagen say irregular migration is "negatively linked to crime rates."
- Politico Europe, 12 hours ago: France, Germany strike bargain on Made in Europe, car emissions.
The compromise was reached after the German Social Democrats, the junior coalition partner in Friedrich Merz’s government, dropped their opposition.

AFRICA

- AllAfrica - Conflict, 18 hours ago: Sudan: Drone Attack Kills Two in North Darfur As Red Crescent Volunteer Killed in Blue Nile.
[Dabanga] Furawiya / Karnoi / El Tina / Umm Darfa / El Rosei -- Drone attack in Furawiya area of North Darfur kills two and injures eight, while a Red Crescent volunteer dies in a bombing in Blue Nile and South Darfur authorities impose sweeping emergency measures.
- Africanews, 10 hours ago: Russian missiles spark huge factory fires in Ukraine’s Odesa and Zaporizhzhia.
Russian strikes ignited massive fires at businesses in Odesa and Zaporizhzhia as President Zelensky met European leaders for talks.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 13 hours ago: Nigeria: Soldiers, Terrorists Killed in Midnight Terror Attack On Borno Military Base.
[Premium Times] Sources said 15 soldiers and five members of the Civilian Joint Task Force (CJTF) were killed in the encounter.
- Africanews, 7 hours ago: Ethiopian gains in Tigray risk wider war with Eritrea, analyst warns.
Ethiopia’s military advances in northern Tigray do not spell an end to the conflict but have the potential to increase the risk of war with neighboring Eritrea, an analyst with knowledge of the region has warned

- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 12 hours ago: South Africa: Katherine O'regan Receives George Bizos Human Rights Award, Warns of Shift to Authoritarianism.
[Daily Maverick] On 15 October, former Constitutional Court Justice Katherine O'Regan received the George Bizos Human Rights Award, reflecting on the project of democracy and urging resistance to rising authoritarianism.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 16 hours ago: Zimbabwe: Poverty, Injustice Threaten Lasting Peace in Zimbabwe - ZPP.
[263Chat] The Zimbabwe Peace Project (ZPP) has called for greater investment in justice, human rights and inclusive institutions warning that poverty, inequality and weak access to justice continue to threaten lasting peace in Zimbabwe.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: PM Shehbaz reaffirms support for Saudi Arabia in meeting with new envoy.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 12 hours ago: PM Shehbaz reaffirms support for Saudi Arabia in meeting with new envoy.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday reaffirmed Pakistan’s support for Saudi Arabia in safeguarding its “sovereignty, security and territorial integrity” amid a recent escalation in Houthi attacks. According to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), the premier made the remarks during a meeting with newly appointed Saudi Ambassador Dr Rajeh Tami Albugamy. He welcomed the envoy to Pakistan and congratulated him on assuming his new responsibilities.
- The Hindu - International, 12 hours ago: Airstrikes, artillery hit north Ethiopia as government and rebels clash, sources say.
Air attacks killed at least 17 people northwest of Tigray’s capital Mekelle — which federal government forces took over the weekend — according to a bulletin circulated among humanitarian groups
- The Hindu - International, 16 hours ago: Drone strikes in the Black Sea raise fears of Russian escalation to test NATO's response.
The attacks in the two countries' exclusive economic zones threaten a global shipping route and have left two people dead, with at least 25 still missing. They also run the risk of drawing other countries directly into the war for Ukraine
- Dawn (Pakistan), 6 hours ago: Kohat Police Lines attack mastermind killed in joint operation in KP's Lakki Marwat: CTD.
LAKKI MARWAT: The Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) said on Friday that its personnel had killed a terrorist commander in a joint operation with security forces in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Lakki Marwat on Friday. The CTD said in a statement that the slain terrorist, whom the law enforcement department identified as Zahid Gul, was the mastermind of the attack on Kohat Police Lines. In the attack on Sept 18, an explosives-laden vehicle detonated near a mosque in Kohat Police Lines, following which terrorists stormed the compound and attacked police facilities.
India - bottom line: Saudi-Led Coalition Intercepts Drones, Missiles Targeted At Riyadh.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 6 hours ago: Saudi-Led Coalition Intercepts Drones, Missiles Targeted At Riyadh.
Since Yemen's civil war flared back to life in July, the Houthis have repeatedly struck Saudi targets including Red Sea tankers, oil facilities and Riyadh's international airport, where 13 people were killed in a single attack last week.
- NDTV - Top Stories, Al Jazeera - Middle East, one hour ago: Yemen's Government-Controlled City Of Aden Attacked In Houthi Strikes.
The attack came a day after the Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen struck a palace complex in Aden, which has been the seat of Yemen's internationally recognized government since 2015.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 7 hours ago: Zelenskyy slams Trump's diesel deal, says will help fund Putin’s war in Ukraine.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has expressed concerns over the US diesel deal with Russia. He warned that this agreement could provide additional funds for Russia's ongoing war against Ukraine. Zelenskyy emphasized the need for Europe to increase support to Ukraine as missile attacks continue. The president requested significant financial assistance to maintain Ukraine's defense against Russian aggression.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 9 hours ago: 'We'll knock it out fast': Trump may target Iran's Pickaxe Mountain nuclear facility.
Donald Trump indicated that the US may target Iran's Pickaxe Mountain facility to deter nuclear weapon development. He stated that nuclear weapons would not be necessary for achieving US objectives in the situation. The remarks followed ongoing US-Israeli strikes against Iran since February, amid rising tensions. Iran's foreign ministry denied any nuclear activity at the site, labeling US threats as baseless.
Asia - bottom line: EU rallies around Zelensky as rift widens with Trump over Russia energy strikes.
- South China Morning Post - China, 13 hours ago: EU rallies around Zelensky as rift widens with Trump over Russia energy strikes.
European leaders on Friday rallied around Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelensky as Kyiv’s ties with US President Donald Trump have nosedived and worries grow that US leader is increasingly siding with Russia. Relations between Kyiv and Washington have soured since last week, when Trump eased sanctions on Russia in exchange for Moscow releasing large amounts of diesel onto global markets. Zelensky infuriated Trump further by ordering Ukraine’s forces to restart strikes on Russian oil refineries in...
- South China Morning Post - China, one hour ago: Oregon teen gunman was tackled by ‘heroic’ teacher then shot by students’ father.
A teacher threw her phone at the teenage gunman who killed four people at an Oregon junior school, then tackled and fought with him – probably saving lives before he was shot by a father who followed him into the building, police said Friday. Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz called the teacher’s actions “heroic” during a news conference and said she was not injured. He identified the attacker as 16-year-old Griffin J. John II and said all of the victims were shot in the same classroom. Authorities...
- South China Morning Post - China, 13 hours ago: China leans in to hi-tech systems to counter emerging AI-fuelled terror threats.
China revealed AI-powered drone interceptors and other uncrewed systems at an international counterterrorism forum in Beijing this week, as security experts warned that new technologies could enable new forms of terrorism. The equipment was on display at the Great Wall-2026 International Forum on Counterterrorism, which ran from Tuesday to Thursday and was attended by more than 320 defence experts and military delegates from 62 countries. Discussions focused on how advances in artificial...
- South China Morning Post - China, 16 hours ago: Envoy says China could ‘easily win’ conflict as Manila claims it is ‘thinly veiled threat’.
Manila has called for diplomatic restraint in response to suggestions from the Chinese ambassador to the Philippines that Beijing could “easily win” a military showdown in the region but had instead chosen peace. The war of words comes amid rising tension over the Scarborough Shoal in the South China Sea. Beijing has repeatedly driven away Philippine aircraft over the shoal in recent months, while accusing Manila of violating Chinese airspace. Ambassador Jing Quan made his comment on Thursday as...

North Korea’s top missile commander accused South Korea of making false claims about a recent hypersonic missile test, according to a short interview released Thursday, drawing a prompt rebuttal from Seoul. DPRK Missile Administration General Director Jang Chang Ha said “It is hard to believe that [South Korea’s hypersonic glide vehicle (HGV)] underwent hypersonic flight” […]

Australia - bottom line: EVs are holding value better than expected – and it has a lot to do with Australia’s cost of living.
- The Guardian - Australia, 9 hours ago: EVs are holding value better than expected – and it has a lot to do with Australia’s cost of living.
The appeal of electric vehicles is financial as much as environmental for many drivers Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here The electric vehicles were splattered after a concrete spray incident, but repairable. Eager to recoup their costs, insurers sent the 40 BYD vehicles to an auction run by asset sales company Pickles in late March. With fuel prices soaring in response to the US and Israel war on Iran, a bidding frenzy erupted. Continue reading...
- ABC News Australia, 3 hours ago: The hearts hoping to create lasting impact at Sculpture by the Sea.
More than 60 hearts, representing women killed in domestic violence incidents, are among the artworks at what is considered the world's biggest outdoor sculpture competition.
- ABC News Australia, one hour ago: Hunt continues for man with shotgun who sparked lockdown in Sydney's inner west.
Residents say they saw a man in a van, which had been stolen from the nearby area a couple of days earlier, who threatened them with a shotgun and set the vehicle alight before fleeing on foot.
- The Guardian - Australia, 9 hours ago: Jim Chalmers’ bad week: an economic dumpster fire and Labor squabbling.
The treasurer is feeling the heat on several fiscal fronts, and some within Labor are questioning the government’s political strategy Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast Jim Chalmers was in Bangkok on Thursday – meeting with finance ministers and central bank governors from around the world – during a 13-hour visit. A grim outlook hung over the talks, which came just days after the International Monetary Fund warned that the global economy “could soon test the limits of resilience”.
